column3: The Hebrew says to give a command to his house and says he will “not live”.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat Hezekiah’s name.
The Hebrew calls the heart whole and emphasizes weeping with the repeated noun “weeping”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “behold, I am healing you”, and does not explicitly add “from now”.
The added years are expressed as being added to his days.
The Hebrew says to take a cake of figs and ends by saying “he lived”, without repeating Hezekiah’s name.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name and speaks of the word He spoke; it does not explicitly add “would you like”.
The Hebrew asks that the shadow turn back: “No, rather let the shadow return backwards ten steps.”
The Hebrew repeats “steps” three times.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says Hezekiah listened to them, without explicitly identifying them as envoys in this clause.
The Hebrew asks first what the men said and then where they came from.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name Isaiah in the question, and uses “house” rather than “palace”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins “behold, days are coming” and uses “house” rather than “palace”.
The Hebrew explicitly says the sons will come forth from him and that he will father them.
The Hebrew says “and he said”, rather than describing a thought. It retains a conditional “if” in the question.
Close to the Hebrew.
Resting is pictured as lying down with his fathers.
